flags.text: Exceptionally high or seemingly risk-free returns are promised
flags.why: Every investment carries risk. 'Guaranteed' high returns are the classic bait.

flags.text: Returns are suspiciously steady, whatever the markets do
flags.why: Real investments go up and down. Smooth gains every month are typical of Ponzi schemes.

flags.text: You are pushed to decide fast: 'only today', 'last places'
flags.why: Urgency stops you from checking. A real opportunity survives a day of thinking.

flags.text: They contacted you first: a call, a message from a 'wrong number', a social media DM
flags.why: The FMA has described unsolicited cold calling for financial transactions as prohibited in Austria and a sure warning sign.

flags.text: Contact happens only through messenger apps or a chat group
flags.why: Fraudsters use WhatsApp, Telegram and chat groups full of fake 'winners' to create trust and pressure.

flags.text: You are asked to install remote access software (e.g. a screen-sharing app)
flags.why: It lets a stranger control your computer and possibly your online banking. No legitimate investment firm needs it.

flags.text: You are asked for passwords, login codes or ID photos
flags.why: With your access data, fraudsters can empty accounts or open new ones in your name.

flags.text: You are told to pay in crypto assets, at a bitcoin ATM, or by transfer to a private person
flags.why: Such payments go straight to the scammers and are very hard to recover.

flags.text: You cannot find the firm in the FMA company database, or it appears on a warning list
flags.why: Anyone offering investment services in Austria needs permission from the FMA.

flags.text: Website, email, phone or address differ from those in the official register
flags.why: Clone firms copy the name and register number of real firms.

flags.text: Your account shows profits, but you must pay 'fees' or 'taxes' before you can withdraw
flags.why: This is advance fee fraud. Every further payment only increases the loss.

flags.text: An online friend or romantic contact you have never met suggests investing
flags.why: Relationship scammers build trust for weeks or months before talking about money.

flags.text: A 'regulator' or 'recovery agency' contacts you and asks for money
flags.why: Regulators do not charge victims fees. Genuine FMA email addresses end only in @fma.gv.at.

flags.text: Celebrities, glowing testimonials or videos 'prove' that others are getting rich
flags.why: Scammers pay for fake reviews and use AI-generated images, videos and voices.

scenarios.message: Hi, is this Martina? Sorry, wrong number! 😊 Nice to meet you anyway. I'm a trader, I make 2% a day with an AI strategy. I could add you to our VIP group, but spots are limited.
scenarios.explain: Wrong-number contact, an unrealistic return (2% a day), a group and artificial scarcity: four red flags in three sentences.

scenarios.message: Alpenrad AG is carrying out a rights issue. You hold 400 shares and receive 400 subscription rights. Please give us your instruction in online banking by 12 November; otherwise the rights may lapse.
scenarios.explain: A normal corporate action notice. It asks you to act in your own online banking, not via a link or a phone call. If in doubt, call your bank using the number on its website, not one from a message.

scenarios.message: Dear investor, the Financial Market Authority has located funds you lost to an online broker. To release €18,400 to you, an anti-money-laundering fee of €1,200 must be paid within 48 hours.
scenarios.explain: Recovery scam with a fake regulator: the domain is not @fma.gv.at, regulators never charge victims fees, and there is a deadline.

scenarios.message: Your first trades went very well! To help you set up the next ones, please install this support app so I can see your screen and guide you through the transfer.
scenarios.explain: A request to install remote access software. No legitimate firm needs to control your device.

scenarios.message: Your monthly savings plan of €100 into the ETF you selected will be executed on the 5th. Fee: 1.5% per execution, as in our price list.
scenarios.explain: Inside an app you installed and opened yourself, about a plan you set up. The fee is disclosed. Still worth checking that the broker is authorised and comparing costs (Category F).

scenarios.message: Congratulations, your balance is now €38,000! Before we can process your withdrawal, please pay the 20% capital gains tax (€7,600) to our tax account.
scenarios.explain: Classic advance fee fraud: 'profits' you cannot withdraw until you pay more. Real taxes are not paid to a trading platform's chat.

checks.title: Is it authorised?
checks.text: Search the FMA company database and check which services the firm may provide.

checks.title: Is there a warning?
checks.text: Search the FMA warning list. A warning means: do not do business with that provider.

checks.title: Is there an international alert?
checks.text: Search IOSCO's I-SCAN, which collects warnings from regulators worldwide (not all independently verified).

checks.title: Do the contact details match?
checks.text: Compare website, email domain, phone number and address with the official register, not with what the firm sent you. Check that the regulator named really exists.
checks.link: FMA on clone firms and fake regulators

checks.title: Still unsure? Ask the regulator.
checks.text: Contact the FMA directly, using contact details from its own website. Never install remote access software or share login codes for anyone.

afterSteps.title: Contact your bank immediately
afterSteps.text: Ask whether payments can be stopped or recalled. The FMA stresses that acting quickly can prevent further damage.

afterSteps.title: Report it to the police
afterSteps.text: File a report (Anzeige) at any police station; the Bundeskriminalamt lists reporting points for online crime.

afterSteps.title: Report the profiles
afterSteps.text: Report the fraudulent profiles and groups to the platforms where you met them.

afterSteps.title: Stop all contact and send no more money
afterSteps.text: Do not respond to new 'offers', including people who claim they can recover your money.

afterSteps.title: Secure your accounts and devices
afterSteps.text: Change passwords. If you installed remote access software, remove it and have the device checked.

afterSteps.title: Keep the evidence
afterSteps.text: Save messages, emails, website addresses, transfer receipts and wallet addresses.

afterSteps.title: Watch out for the second wave
afterSteps.text: Recovery scams target previous victims, often posing as regulators or law firms. Never pay to get your money back.
